cause_quote: The Telnyx greeting fix added `shouldStartListeningAfterInitialMessage`, whose `if (!ctx.config.streaming.enabled) { return true; }` branch made speakInitialMessage call `ctx.provider.startListening(...)` for Twilio non-streaming calls, sending a bare Gather TwiML update that replaces the Say greeting just sent by playTts.
user_saw: On Twilio conversation calls without media streams the caller heard silence instead of the greeting, and the call hung up about five seconds after a reply if the caller did not speak right away.
summary: Twilio fallback playback now sends Say followed by a 120-second Gather with a signed silence redirect in one TwiML update, skipping the separate startListening update that cut playback, and renews listening on silence.
reasoning: At 455e84f77694's tree Twilio playTts already sent Say followed by Gather, and speakInitialMessage did not call startListening afterward; that commit (aimed at Telnyx) added the conversation-mode startListening for every non-streaming provider including Twilio, which is the greeting loss reported in #158262. The second symptom (5-second Gather default timeout and continueCall's speak-then-startListening) is older code that never handled silence, so the fix mixes a regression with a never-worked part; medium confidence because I did not exhaustively rule out other pre-April startListening callers.
